task: Task 6 step 6 (6C): blobs producing no accepted facet, canonical 2026-07-26 state
instrument: find_roof_planes now takes a peel_log and records EVERY plane it peels, with its pitch, BEFORE the pitch window filters it. Previously that filter was silent, so a blob yielding no facet could not be told apart from a blob where RANSAC found nothing at all. Those are different diagnoses and only one of them is a problem.

blobs.why_no_facet: every surface here is near-FLAT (8.2 deg, below the 10.0 deg minimum). This is a low-slope surface sitting outside the roof-facet definition, not a facet the fit failed to find.
mixed: 3 near-vertical (89.1, 88.5, 87.6 deg) and 1 near-flat (6.1 deg) surface(s), none inside the 10.0-60.0 deg roof window
every surface here is near-VERTICAL (89.1, 88.6 deg, above the 60.0 deg maximum). Vertical surfaces are not roof facets: they are dormer cheeks, gable ends or wall tops. Nothing is missing here.

every surface here is near-VERTICAL (88.2, 84.3, 65.7 deg, above the 60.0 deg maximum). Vertical surfaces are not roof facets: they are dormer cheeks, gable ends or wall tops. Nothing is missing here.

interpretation: A residual blob is unexplained PLAN AREA. It is not automatically a missing roof facet. Coverage is a plan-view test, so a vertical surface standing inside the footprint (a dormer cheek, a gable end) occupies plan cells whose points belong to no roof facet, and registers as a gap that no roof facet can ever close. Those blobs are a permanent floor on coverage, not a defect.
